task.description: Validate src/design/iss0617-gbl134-missing-tables-followup.md, which designs a NEW forward migration GBL-136 to complete GBL-134's incomplete GLOBAL_REGISTRY table drop (13 missing table names, listed in the design). This is a database migration touching a table set already affected by ISS-0620's separate data-loss finding -- scrutinize carefully. Verify: (1) the exact 13-name list matches docs/issue-reports/ISS-0185-diagnosis.yaml's classification precisely -- cross-check yourself, do not trust the design doc's transcription; (2) the 4 ISS-0620-flagged names (artifact_activation_groups, entity_definitions, entity_record_latest, entity_type_instances) are genuinely absent from GBL-136's table list; (3) the FK-dependency analysis is correct -- independently query pg_constraint (or read the relevant table-creation migrations) to confirm artifact_versions genuinely has live FK dependents from PER_TENANT tables (artifact_activations, artifact_activation_history) that make it permanently un-droppable via RESTRICT, and confirm tenant_hostnames -> tenant is the only in-scope-to-in-scope dependency requiring drop ordering; (4) the exception-handling design (wrapping each drop in its own BEGIN...EXCEPTION WHEN dependent_objects_still_exist...END so one un-droppable table doesn't abort the whole migration) is a genuine, necessary deviation from GBL-134's bare structure -- confirm GBL-134's original pattern really would abort the whole transaction on a RESTRICT failure (read GBL-134's actual DO $$ block structure to confirm no existing exception handling); (5) the flagged GBL-135 discrepancy (claims 5 names reclassified PER_TENANT with public copies dropped, but design says live inspection shows all 5 public copies still exist) -- verify this claim yourself too, since if true it may need its own incidental-discovery filing (do not file it yourself, just confirm/deny it exists so ORCH can decide); (6) confirm no production code or test files are touched -- this should be pure migration design. RE-CHECK: CODE-DESIGNER reworked the design after your BLOCKER finding -- corrected GBL-136 scope from 13 to 8 tables (artifact_versions, event_type_registry_producers, oidc_migration_item, oidc_migration_job, registry_idp_operation_ledger, repository_artifacts, tenant, tenant_hostnames), excluding the 5 names GBL-135 already resolved in the PER_TENANT direction. Also added the missing FK dependent (repository_form_schemas -> artifact_versions) and corrected Section 6 to note TC-EXP-601-04s second failure mode (instance_waits) is no longer fixed by this design since that table is now out of scope. Re-validate from scratch: independently re-verify the corrected 8-name list against GBL-135s actual v_tables array and the original 13-name computation, confirm the FK addition is accurate, and confirm the Section 6 scope-narrowing claim is consistent with the rest of the document.
acceptance_criteria: The 13-name table list independently verified correct against the diagnosis file
ISS-0620s 4 flagged names confirmed absent from GBL-136s scope
FK-dependency analysis (artifact_versions un-droppable, tenant_hostnames->tenant ordering) independently verified against pg_constraint or source, not trusted
Exception-handling deviation from GBL-134s pattern confirmed necessary (not a fabricated justification)
GBL-135 discrepancy claim independently checked (confirm or deny, do not file anything)
No production code or test files touched

result.summary: Re-checked reworked design after rework 1/3. Independently recomputed the 13-name gap (diagnosis 37-name list minus GBL-134's 24-name v_tables) and confirmed the 4 ISS-0620 names are absent from it. Independently recomputed 13 minus GBL-135's actual 12-name v_tables overlap (5 names: api_token_audit, event_payload_store, instance_definition_snapshots, instance_waits, variable_schemas) = 8 remaining names, and confirmed exact match to the design's claimed 8-name GBL-136 scope (artifact_versions, event_type_registry_producers, oidc_migration_item, oidc_migration_job, registry_idp_operation_ledger, repository_artifacts, tenant, tenant_hostnames). repository_artifacts (GH-566 root cause) confirmed in scope. Live pg_constraint query against tenant_default on bpm_test confirmed all FK edges in the design's table exactly, including the newly-added fk_form_schema_version (repository_form_schemas.version_id -> artifact_versions.version_id, ON DELETE CASCADE) and the sole artifact_versions -> repository_artifacts edge (direction confirms repository_artifacts is undropped-blocking-free). Confirmed tenant has exactly one local dependent (tenant_hostnames) and registry_idp_operation_ledger exists in neither schema, matching the design's claims. Section 6's instance_waits correction is internally consistent across the whole document -- no stale contradictory claim found. Only design/handoff artefacts changed on this branch; no production or test files touched. lint_design_artefact.py exits 0 (BLOCKER=0 MAJOR=0 MINOR=4, all MINOR schema-qualification style notes).
